1.explanation: Each of these Skeleton components renders a <label> tag with htmlFor but no child text (or aria-label), so the label has no accessible name. To fix the DAP violation, the label must include descriptive text or be hidden properly (e.g. using aria-hidden or visually hidden text) so that assistive tools can identify the associated input. These four files are the core instances of the empty-label pattern and must be updated to supply accessible text.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering the various „skeleton“ loading placeholders for Checkbox, NumberInput, Select, Slider, TextArea and TextInput, each component emits a <label> element with no inner text or accessible name. DAP flags this as “Provide descriptive text in LABEL elements” because an empty or self-closing <label> cannot identify the expected input. The screenshots for Checkbox, NumberInput, Select, TextArea and TextInput all show a blank skeleton shape with the DAP violation next to an empty <label>.
